newsitem.title: INDIA: India trust vote set for April 11 - minister.
newsitem.headline: India trust vote set for April 11 - minister.

text.p: India's parliament will meet on April 11 to consider a vote of confidence in the ruling United Front coalition which lost vital support this week, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Srikanta Jena said on Wednesday.
"The session is on the 11th. The vote of confidence will be on that day," Jena told Reuters by telephone.
On Monday, President Shankar Dayal Sharma asked Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda to call a vote of confidence by April 11.
Jena confirmed that the vote, required because the Congress party had withdrawn support for Deve Gowda, would take place on the 11th.

He said that for the moment, the trust vote was the only item on the agenda of the lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, on April 11. Political parties, however, were considering putting the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to a vote before a confidence vote.
Deve Gowda, whose 15-party United Front coalition controls 180 votes in the 545-seat Lok Sabha, would have to win a simple majority to survive the trust vote.
